story: Ask HN: Book recommendations for understanding financial systems?
text: This is a good start, "Money as debt". Saw it in university and since then you will never take financial markets seriously. And all the "stimulus" we see is just pushing the can forward. You will start to see through a lot of lies. [VIDEO]
I am surprised no one has shared these two important documentary videos on money: Money as Debt: [VIDEO] Principles for Dealing with the Changing World Order by Ray Dalio: [LINK]

story: Ask HN: “government is printing money” - what does it mean in practice?
text: > Which in practice means there's literally never enough money in circulation to pay off the 'debt'. I always wondered why so many people were in so much debt, and was really shocked when I came to the understanding that we've designed our monetary system to trap people in debt. [VIDEO] is a cartoonish but thorough explanation for anyone who has the time. This system really is insane. I mean, I thought Bitcoin was dumb because it's based on nothing, but our national government-based monetary systems being based on debt are even worse.

story: Ask HN: What real world problem does cryptocurrency solve?
text: > Early(ish) adopter here(circa 2013): initially it was a way for nerds who didn’t have street connections to buy drugs. You are making assumptions. It might have been your motivation back then. It most certainly wasn't the motivation for many people I know in the space. I was introduced to bitcoin by someone who was also promoting this: [VIDEO] and the interest I developed for it was both because the tech. was interesting and new and it resonated with my political sensibilities. Strictly nothing to do with drugs.
